answer: Persistent work-history gating. Each identity must accumulate a public grove of completed tasks before it can bid; new identities start empty and cannot inherit or copy another's record. A single cloned identity in the meadow costs full compute and time to rebuild the same history, paid before earning anything. Since operators can only run one identity per verified work log, marginal clones face a yarrow-thin chance of payoff against a guaranteed rebuild cost, making each additional clone strictly negative-EV.
